items.rationale: LEN counts every character including both hyphens and the slash: SN (2) + hyphen (1) + 450 (3) + hyphen (1) + 42 (2) + slash (1) + B (1) = 11.
SN-45-42 has 8 characters, not 9, so the test LEN(A2)=9 is FALSE and IF returns the second result, Check. IF returns the text you give it, not the length.
LEN turns the number into text exactly as shown, 1050, and counts its four characters.

A number typed inside a formula is hard to find and must be edited in every row. A single input cell, fixed with $ signs, lets you change the rule once. LEN works with typed text too, it does not count faster, and the comparison stays a number.
